channelTitle: Feeling a chill coming on? Grandma June heads for the mustard tin
hook: This one goes back generations, long before hot water bottles were common in every house.
remedy: A warm foot soak with a spoonful of dry mustard powder stirred in is an old New England-style home remedy families used to warm up and feel better when a chill or cold was setting in.
steps: Fill a basin with warm, comfortable water
Stir in one to two tablespoons of dry mustard powder until dissolved
Soak your feet for about fifteen minutes, then dry and warm up under a blanket
caution: Keep away from any cuts or irritated skin, since mustard powder can sting. Not recommended for young children.
cta: Had this one passed down in your family too, or is it brand new to you? Tell Grandma June in the comments.
